contract: SubagentFactory is a unit that turns an agent type and a prompt into a running child session
SubagentContextBuilder is a unit that decides what the child sees (prompt, tools, inherited state) and what comes back to the parent
SubagentScheduler is a unit that admits, tracks, wakes, cancels, and resumes subagents

The model sees one subagent-spawning tool, task; a call passes gates in order (rewind and dispose state, agent type, disabled and excluded lists, model policy, depth, concurrency), builds the child from a plan, and registers it in the task store
The child is a full session with depth above zero, its own system prompt from the agent definition and a filtered tool set; its only task context is the prompt the parent wrote
A sync call returns the child final message as the tool result; a background call returns an agent id at once and read_agent or a notification turn brings the result back
Policy is computed as data plus an ordered effect list (plan then effects); only effects that need live host objects are applied host side

Host effect vocabulary is start_subagent with five sub-actions, custom_agent_prompt, custom_agent_system_prompt, permission_request_handler, system_prompt_section_transform, has_active_background_work and three factory_* effects
start_subagent sub-actions are prepareTools, resolveSubconscious, resolveRubberDuckRollout, resolveSelectedModel, checkStartAllowed; any other action fails "Unsupported start-subagent host action"
A session is a child exactly when its subagent depth is above zero (isSubagentSession)
Agent id is the child instance id (a UUID) and is the envelope agentId on child events and the agent_id that read_agent takes
Tool call id is the parent toolCallId for the task call, carried on subagent.started
Task registry id (taskRegistryAgentId) is the task-store node id; subagent.started.data.parentId holds the spawner registry id and is absent for a root spawn
A child has its own native session id distinct from its agent id
Depth is zero for the root session and above zero for a child
The bridge copies a child events onto the parent stream stamped with the child agentId
The task tool takes agent_type, name, description, prompt, mode and optionally model and a context tier
Invalid mode or context_tier arguments fail with a schema validation error naming the field
session.tasks.startAgent takes agentType, prompt, name, optional description and model, returns agentId, background only with no mode field
execution_subagent and search_subagent tools each have their own model flag and turn cap, not the task model argument
/rubber-duck and fleet mode inject prompts telling the model to call task; they are not constructors
rem-agent in process is a task call with the rem-agent type; out of process shutdown spawns a new root session marked COPILOT_DETACHED_SESSION
Workflow agents are a separate entry with their own accounting
Custom agents are agent_type values that task resolves, not a separate entry
Start gates run before creation: rewind or dispose state, init check, initialized check, model cache check, ensure agent start allowed
Factory asks the host for start gate, selected model and rollout flags through start_subagent host actions
Agent type resolves against registry and policy lists, depth and concurrency are checked, then the model resolves
A planner produces construction options and an effect list for the child
The child gets a native session of its own with a session id distinct from agent ids and the root session id
Post-start steps copy loaded skills from the parent, refresh the skill catalog, recompose tool metadata, link telemetry lineage and inherit response limits
The child is registered in the task store, subagent.started is emitted, then its first turn begins
Creation is refused while blocksSubagentStart (rewind operation active or disposing) is set
Before planning, the MCP tool snapshot refresh waits for the catalog and pending tool changes, builds tools of servers this session owns and merges them with already inherited tools
A rewind or dispose beginning during the MCP refresh restores the previous snapshot
MCP refresh failure logs "Failed to refresh MCP tools before subagent creation" and creation continues
The plan request carries the child agent id, public session id, default integration id, caller options and a parent view (MCP server configs, workspace path, parent registry id)
The plan reply carries constructionOptions and effects; a missing required field fails "subagent creation plan is missing required field"
The host adds live objects that cannot cross the plan boundary before creating the session
File-change tracking is refused for a session without local storage, but only at depth zero
Only a depth-zero session installs the limiter and task analytics; a child never configures a limiter
Effect invalidateAgentToolConfig clears the child cached tool config and the rubber-duck availability scalar
Effect seedIfc does nothing
Effect inheritMcpTools selects which parent MCP tools the child keeps (those from servers it does not own)
Effect inheritContentExclusion shares the parent content-exclusion service without ownership
Effect emitStarted emits subagent.started on the parent with the child agent id as envelope id
Effect bridgeEvents starts the event bridge pump
Effect notifyCompletion installs a completion callback on the child
Effect bridgeCallbacks forwards callback-runtime events to the parent when eventsLogIncludesSubagents is set
Built-in agent types are general-purpose, explore, task, code-review, security-review, research, rubber-duck and rem-agent
general-purpose has no model field, uses session tools and its prompt cannot be overridden
explore declares models [gpt-5.6-luna, gpt-5.4-mini] with effort low and a read-only tool list (grep, glob, view, bash, lsp, GitHub MCP read tools); first available model wins
task declares models [gpt-5.6-luna, gpt-5.4-mini, claude-haiku-4.5] with all tools and shares the tool name
code-review and security-review declare no model and all tools
research declares the single model string claude-sonnet-5 and all tools
rubber-duck declares no model (dynamic) and all tools
rem-agent declares no model and only the context_board tool, and its description says not to invoke it spontaneously
Agent definitions carry name, displayName, description, model (string or ordered list), reasoningEffort, tools, promptParts and prompt
Custom agents add modelPolicy, models, userInvocable, disableModelInvocation, mcpServers, skills, source and path
Custom agents are discovered from ~/.copilot/agents, .github/agents and the organization .github repository
Serving a custom agent prompt refuses an agent that is not in the available custom agent list
Function-valued custom agent prompts are kept in a sidecar map and served as prompt and system prompt text on request
An unknown agent_type fails "Unknown agent_type: {x}. Valid types are: {list}"

Session includedBuiltinAgents and excludedBuiltinAgents filter built-ins; errors say excluded by, or not included by, this session's configuration; an excluded built-in stays hidden unless a custom agent has the same name
subagents.disabledSubagents refuses dispatch with an error ending "Enable it in /subagents before dispatching it."; listing drops disabled names only for disableable built-ins
Rubber-duck is offered only with builtInAgents.rubberDuck or the rubber-duck experiment; the subconscious flag gates rem-agent availability
A policy refresh clears a selected custom agent that became unavailable and invalidates the tool configuration
Custom agents opt into repository instruction files with include-custom-instructions: true in frontmatter; built-in agents set includeCustomAgentInstructions false
Settings entries under subagents.agents.<agent_type> hold model, modelPolicy (preferred or required), effortLevel, contextTier (inherit, default, long_context) and autoInvoke
updateSubagentSettings applies live settings overrides to the session
subagent.started reports modelSelectionSource from explicit_override, configured_required, configured_preference, complementary_default, session_inheritance, agent_definition_default, runtime_policy
subagent.started reports taskModelSource from task_argument, subagent_configuration, custom_agent_definition, unset
A required settings model beats both the YAML model candidates and YAML reasoning effort; the child runs on it with configured_required and subagent_configuration
An explicit model argument, a preferred setting and the YAML list are ordered by the provenance enums (explicit over preferred over definition)
A candidate that exceeds the cost guard for the session or is missing from the available list is skipped
If no candidate survives the child falls back to the session model; a custom provider or auto-mode session changes the fallback
A required model that fails the cost guard is a hard error ending "exceeds the allowed cost relative to the current session model" with no fallback
A requested model that conflicts with a required policy is silently replaced ("Required model enforcement replaced requested model")
A complementary Auto session must exist before the complementary model is acquired
The model catalog carries a subagentOnlyModels partition
Contextual tier long_context and effortLevel from settings or the agent definition reach the child (reasoningEffort and tier reported in subagent.configured)
Task subagents may get readable ids such as math-helper-0 in the changelog but live children use UUID agent ids; the name argument is the agentDisplayName
taskRegistryAgentId is a separate id; the plan request carries the parent and the child stores the caller
toolCallId is provisional for background tasks rebuilt from the event log until the started event envelope id supplies the canonical id
The prompt-cache lineage id passes from parent to child and defaults to the root native id
Local and AHP backends log with native-subagent: and ahp-subagent: prefixes

Child model requests carry X-Interaction-Type conversation-subagent, X-Agent-Task-Id (child agent id), X-Parent-Agent-Id and X-Client-Session-Id (root session id) and the body repeats agent_task_id and parent_agent_id
Starting while rewinding or disposing fails "Cannot start subagent while the session is rewinding or disposing"
The task gate fails "Cannot start a task while the session is rewinding or disposing"
Missing session tools fail "Cannot start subagent: tools are not available for this session"
An unknown start-subagent host action fails "Unsupported start-subagent host action"
Unknown type, depth, disabled, excluded and cost guard refusals come from the task tool with the quoted strings
A failing event bridge reports "Subagent event bridge failed"
The subagentStart hook runs when a subagent is spawned and cannot block creation
Task context is only the parent-written prompt prefixed with a current-datetime tag; no parent history
The child system prompt is built from the agent definition plus promptParts flags; the parent system message is not copied except for general-purpose
Child tools are the definition tools list intersected with session filters (availableTools, excludedTools, toolFilterPrecedence); parent restrictions persist
The parent MCP tools are snapshotted before each spawn and the child keeps those from servers it does not own
Skills are copied from the parent after creation; skills on a custom agent load eagerly
The parent content-exclusion service object is shared with the child
A hook processor is forked per child and keyed by the child agent id
Child permission requests route to the parent permission flow
A plan-mode write gate is a live callback to the parent
The parent can only restrict web search for the child; a parent override with enabled false wins
Feature flags are shared, plugin and trust snapshots are copied, the session filesystem is shared and a child is not a separate rewind point
Memory is a capability the planner may omit; when absent a capability_absent_subagent telemetry record is made
Response limits are inherited and maxAgentTurns, lastTurnWarning, maxOutputTokens and sessionLimits ride on construction options
disabledInstructionSources comes from the plan, not the parent; built-in agents set includeCustomAgentInstructions to false
Telemetry and prompt cache lineage are linked to the root
The child system prompt opens with the agent definition prompt and then holds the sections tools, prohibited_actions, tool_calling, subagent_usage, environment_context in that order
The tools section carries notes for rg, view and bash with the shell_security note nested in the bash part and two examples
environment_context is last and holds the working directory, git repository root, operating system name, a directory snapshot and available tools
promptParts includeAISafety enables prohibited_actions; includeToolInstructions enables the tools block; includeParallelToolCalling enables the end-of-prompt parallel-calling text
promptParts includeEnvironmentContext enables environment_context and cwdListing is a string name controlling the directory listing

promptParts includeDynamicContextBoard, includeSessionSearchContext, includeCloudSessionSearchContext, includeConsolidationPrompt and includeOutputChannelInstructions enable the context board, session search, rem consolidation and sidekick inbox wording
promptParts includeCustomInstructions and includeCustomAgentInstructions gate repository and agent instructions; all built-ins set the second to false

All built-ins set includeAISafety and includeToolInstructions true; all but rem-agent set includeEnvironmentContext true; rem-agent sets environment context and parallel calling false and includeConsolidationPrompt true
Template variables {{grepToolName}}, {{globToolName}} and {{shellToolName}} are substituted and grep resolves to rg

Subagents get "As a sub-agent, complete your parent's task yourself; use another general-purpose agent only if the parent explicitly requests nested delegation."; background or headless children get a non-interactive preamble
general-purpose is built from the main agent prompt inputs ("general-purpose prompt omitted systemMessage")
The SDK systemMessage option customizes twelve named sections through the system_prompt_section_transform effect; the child systemMessage is the per-call option, not the parent
The child subagent_usage block opens "Default to doing the work yourself." and repeats the three parent bullets
The explore child prompt opens "You are an exploration agent. Answer the question as fast as possible, then stop."
subagent.selected reports the definition declared tools, not the effective child tools
The effective tool set can differ from the declared one (grep renamed to rg, list_bash added, PowerShell, lsp and MCP names dropped)
Tool initialization runs stages tool_init_subagent_preferences, tool_init_requested_tools, tool_init_inherited_mcp_tools, subagent_tool_filter, subagent_tool_surface_prepare
Update options subagentToolPolicyExact and preserveSubagentToolFilters keep later option updates from overwriting a child computed filters
Flag copilot_cli_task_subagent_aggressive_tool_deferral defers tools in task children to a tool-search step and ToolSearchConfig.deferThreshold defaults to 30 tools
Context-management tools (session_artifacts, get_context_remaining, session_history, new_context) reach a subagent only when subagents.contextManagementTools is on
MCP inheritance on spawn snapshots the parent MCP tools including ones the parent inherited so a grandchild sees inherited and owned tools; servers the child own definition configures are excluded
The GitHub MCP tool configuration and user override are copied; the OAuth store is shared only with preserveMcpOAuthStoreOnHostReplacement
Configured skill preloading fails "subagent requested skills but the parent session has no loaded skills"
A skills copy failure reports "failed to copy parent skills onto subagent session"

The child permission handler delegates to the parent: the parent attributes the request to the child, runs permission routing with hooks and either asks its own parent or answers directly; managed policy can force a re-ask
User-input and elicitation requests from children are mediated through the parent (request_subagent_user_input)
Hook types subagentStart and subagentStop exist and the stop hook input includes a transcript path
A child hook processor is forked with the child agent id and a child created with an empty agent id warns
Hook events from inside a subagent are re-emitted on the parent
Extension permission handlers approve subagent requests without duplicate prompts
Start hook contexts combine within the output limit
Three channels carry results back: the tool result string, bridged events on the parent stream and task-store state for read_agent, the task UI and the SDK
A sync task result is the child final assistant message verbatim with identical detailed content
A background task result begins "Agent started in background with agent_id: {id}. You'll be notified when it completes." and tells the model to say it is waiting or continue unrelated work

The background result adds that the agent supports multi-turn conversations and that write_agent suits only same-task follow-ups; its detailed content is "Prompt to explore agent ({id})" then the prompt

read_agent with wait true after completion returns "Agent is idle (waiting for messages)." then agent_id, agent_type, status, description, elapsed, total_turns and a "[Turn 0]" section with the child reply
A finished background agent reports idle, not completed, because multi-turn agents stay alive for follow-ups

Result strings: "Agent completed but produced no response.", the suffix " Use read_agent to check for results." after a move to background and the memory-retired form "Agent was retired after completing its turn to free memory and cannot receive follow-up messages."
Boundary markers (begin, end, failed "All messages from here to ...") annotate the flattened events log with best-effort stack attribution and a concurrent-sibling misattribution warning
The bridge delivers each child event to the parent with suppressedBridgeEvents, as an external-tool service call or as emit or emitEphemeral with the child agent id
Child events reach the JSONL stream and the persisted session log with the child agentId (15 events per child)
COPILOT_EVENTS_LOG_INCLUDE_SUBAGENTS sets eventsLogIncludesSubagents only for the string true but child events persist regardless
The parent prompt carries a subagent_usage block that says to default to doing the work yourself and use custom agents sparingly
Heuristics: "Do not delegate work you can finish in five or fewer direct tool calls." and "Use background mode only while doing independent work; do not poll."
Heuristics: wait guidance after a background launch, no fixed write_agent worker pool for batches, and read_agent with since_turn for only new responses

A subagent_model_preferences block lists the /subagents preferences and says not to copy them into task calls unless the user or instructions require an explicit model; required entries are enforced anyway
The task tool header is "Launch specialized agents in separate context windows for specific tasks." followed by the available types, user custom agents and statelessness notes
Rubber-duck guidance says to call it synchronously after planning and before implementation and a security-review caller contract exists
A session-scoped limiter configures maxConcurrent and maxDepth once at the root session (configureSubAgentLimiter)
The limiter wrapper offers tryAcquireSubAgent (a string error becomes {error, limitType: "concurrent"}), releaseSubAgent and getSubAgentLimiterInfo
A nested spawn reaches the root limiter; nested subagents respect concurrency limits
The default maximum sub-agent depth is 4
subagents.maxConcurrency and subagents.maxDepth are integers from 1 to 128 and the schema declares no default
The default concurrency number is computed at session construction and is not specified by the source
A later sessionApplySubagentSettings does not reconfigure the limiter
Spawn at the limit is rejected "Maximum concurrent agent limit of {N} reached. Wait for existing agents to complete before spawning new ones."
Resume at the limit is rejected "Cannot resume agent" + em dash + "all {N} concurrent agent slots are in use. Try again after an active agent completes." with no agent id
Depth at the limit is rejected "Maximum sub-agent depth of {N} reached. Complete this task without spawning further sub-agents."
Admission is a hard reject with no queue for the session limiter
A resumed idle agent needs a free slot so an idle agent holds none
Sync is the default; a sync task call returns when the child finishes, is promoted to background or times out
Sync task calls block until completion instead of auto-promoting to background after 60 seconds
getAgentResult can return a result, {promoted: true} or {timedOut: true}
A background call returns an agent id at once; the driver failure text is "Subagent background driver failed unexpectedly"
Promotion moves a sync task to background while the original wait is open (promoteCurrentToBackground); empty result text "No running sync task to move to background."
canPromoteToBackground is true only during the original sync wait and getCurrentPromotable returns the first sync-waiting task, agents before shells
Two task calls (one sync, one background) in one parent turn run concurrently and their results are emitted together at the end of the parallel batch

The task registry wraps the task store with register, get, list, cancel, complete, fail, remove, children, start agent, agent result, send message, wait for message, enter idle, promote, progress mutation and transition subscription
The store is keyed by taskStoreId which for a session equals its native session id; public task kinds are agent, shell and client
Task statuses are running, idle, completed, failed, cancelled; memory-retired is not a status
Transitions: registered to running, running to idle on turn end, idle to running on write_agent delivery, running to completed/failed/cancelled, idle to cancelled
Transitions reach the host as task_transition events and the base session emits the ephemeral session.background_tasks_changed when a transition should notify
Task transitions are serialized through a dispatch flow
Progress updates mutate agent progress for setting intent, counting tool calls, updating MCP tasks and recording executor telemetry
read_agent takes agent_id, wait (default false), timeout (default 30 seconds, maximum 180) and since_turn (inclusive)
write_agent sends a follow-up and accepts only background agents in running or idle state, failing otherwise with messages such as "write_agent only supports background agents"
list_agents discovers agents and a scope matching too many agents fails with a message that the match "exceeds the limit of" a number and asks for an explicit agent_ids list
A message sent during rewind or dispose is refused "Cannot deliver a task message while the session is rewinding or disposing"
session.tasks.sendMessage reaches the same store
For a background child, completion becomes a system notification of kind agent_completed (terminal), agent_idle (multi-turn waiting) or new_inbox_message (sidekick or hook inbox)
The UI text for agent_idle still says completed
A completion wake is queued as enqueueResumePending and counts as active work that blocks rewind
When a background child finishes the log records `Agent "{name}" ({type}) has finished processing and is now idle.`
Redundant notifications are avoided after a blocking read_agent returns
Session idle is deferred while background work exists and predicates can be registered (registerBackgroundWorkPredicate)
Non-interactive runs wait for background tasks before exit with timeout COPILOT_TASK_WAIT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS and the message "waiting for background tasks to finish; exiting"
Completion hooks emit subagent.completed or subagent.failed from a planned completion
The event bridge pumps child progress to the parent and falls back to durable progress when an ordered flush fails ("ordered native subagent bridge flush failed; falling back to durable progress")
Teardown reports "timed out waiting for subagent participant cleanup"
blocksSubagentStart is rewindOperationActive or disposing and beginning a rewind blocks agent start
Rewind is refused while any agent runs or a cancelled execution is draining (task tree or sidekick tree), while a resume wake is queued, or while the user message queue is non-empty
cancelProcessing runs actions cancelSidekicks, cancelActiveAgents and drainPendingRequests
cancelAllBackgroundAgents cancels sidekicks and then background agents
Dispose sets disposing, blocks new starts, waits for rewind and shell operations to quiesce and runs the dispose ladder
Cancellation completes, it does not fail: subagent.completed carries cancelled true
Superseded runs count as cancellations
Teardown failure reports "failed to join background subagent during session teardown"
cancelActiveAgents can include idle agents
Session resume does not replay subagents; the runtime closes interrupted subagent records ("Closed interrupted sub-agent records on resume") with a repair step
The repair routine also runs at shutdown and logs closed and dangling counters
resumable on subagent.started is always false
Journaled workflow subagent results are preserved so a workflow resume reuses them
Sidekicks are an adjacent scheduler with a separate task store initialized through the initializeSidekick effect; rewind and hasActiveWork consult both stores
Abort, suspend and model-cache invalidation cancel all sidekicks

Sidekick YAML holds triggers (user.message, session.context_changed, session.memory_changed), per-trigger limit, behavior (persistent or restart), cancelOnNewTurn, maxSendsPerTurn, featureFlag, launchConditions, inlineForwardMaxChars
Five production sidekick definitions ship gated by flags: subconscious-agent (COPILOT_SUBCONSCIOUS, persistent), github-context and github-context-memory, session-search and cloud-session-search
Sidekick results arrive as new_inbox_message notifications and through the send_inbox tool, not read_agent
A sidekick trigger limit reports "Sidekick trigger limit reached"
autoInvoke is not a sidekick flag; only the built-in rubber-duck consumes it
The session queue scheduler defers session idle while background work exists and turns a completion wake into a parent turn
The scheduler root owns the future that runs a subagent execution; an unplanned cancel reports "scheduler-root task was cancelled unexpectedly"
A workflow is a function written with defineWorkflow and registered by an extension; the runtime supervises it and each ctx.agent(prompt, opts) call becomes one workflow-scoped subagent
Declarations pass validation and are silently dropped when dynamicWorkflowsEnabled is false; registration installs a resolver and a metadata provider and a disconnect unregisters them

The model starts a workflow with run_dynamic_workflow after a user permission prompt of kind workflow showing effective and declared limits; pre-checks cover argument shape, name conflicts and the active-run cap
A run row moves from pending to running by compare-and-set with effective limits persisted and a lease with an owner epoch refreshed by a heartbeat
Execution sends resolve-provider then execute to the extension and a stale execution token is rejected
ctx.phase and ctx.log buffer into a log, ctx.step uses the journal, ctx.agent spawns a subagent, and a pause or ctx.pause(key) records a checkpoint and moves the run to paused
A run settles as completed, halted, paused, cancelled or error; workflow.run_settled fires and the factory_completed notification normalizes to workflow_completed

Resume reloads name, arguments, journal, accounting and approved limits, increments the attempt and replays journaled steps; a pending or running run with a different owner epoch and an expired lease flips to error with reason interrupted and can be resumed; extension disconnect halts runs
Run statuses are pending, running, completed, halted, paused, cancelled and error
Workflow state persists in tables factory_runs, factory_progress, factory_phases, factory_agents, factory_journal (keyed by root run id) and factory_credit_charges
Limits maxConcurrentSubagents, maxTotalSubagents, timeoutSeconds and maxAiCredits resolve from declared limits, then configured defaults (workflows.defaultLimits), then per-run overrides
Admission atomically increments consumed_subagents only while below maxTotal and a guarded decrement rolls back failed preparation so concurrent ctx.parallel branches cannot overshoot
maxAiCredits is a soft post-paid ceiling so completed or parallel turns can settle above it
Hitting the total, time or credit limit ends the run as error with failure type workflow_limit_reached and the run can resume with a raised limit while consumption is retained
Extra workflow subagents wait in a queue and queueing does not fail the run; a closed limiter reports "Factory subagent limiter is closed"
A schema call retries once on a parse or match failure so it may spawn twice and both spawns count toward maxTotalSubagents
Workflow agents use the dedicated entry point and share the subagent machinery; subagent.started carries workflowRunId and the legacy factoryRunId

Workflow agents have their own per-run limiter and are hidden from the task registry views, read_agent, write_agent and /tasks; started events carrying a workflow run id are dropped when tasks are rebuilt
Factory is the internal name of Dynamic Workflows and the public name is workflow; a workflows slash command exists and the legacy factoryRunId field survives
Pause and resume workflow runs from the /factories dialog
The workflows UI is gated by the EXTENSIONS flag and the quota fields dynamicWorkflowsEnabled and dynamicWorkflowsUiVisible
Workflow run settings: workflows.maxConcurrentRuns (default 4, range 1 to 16), workflows.logPhaseNames, workflows.defaultLimits

Workflow SDK surface: session.workflow run, resume, getRun, listRuns, getRunDetail, getRunProgress, cancel, pause, log, agent, journal.get, journal.put and client-hosted workflow.execute and workflow.abort
Workflow agents take options mirroring subagents.agents.* (WorkflowAgentOptions)
A workflow run lifecycle tool surface: run_dynamic_workflow, dynamic_workflows_manage and read_workflow_run
The sync task walkthrough: gates and host actions, resolve type and policy, check depth and concurrency, resolve model, plan, create child, register task, emit subagent.started
Walkthrough event order on the parent is subagent.started, session.background_tasks_changed, subagent.configured, subagent.selected
The child receives one user message holding a datetime tag and the parent prompt and its model request carries the subagent headers
The child final message becomes the task result and subagent.completed fires with token and duration totals
The parent tool.execution_complete carries the child message as the tool result and the parent model continues
Subagent events are durable session events (optional ephemeral flag) and session.background_tasks_changed is the always-ephemeral one; the envelope agentId marks child-owned events
Envelope parentId links the previous event in the chain and data.parentId names the spawning task registry id

subagent.started data: toolCallId, agentName, agentDisplayName, agentDescription, model, taskModelSource, modelSelectionSource, resumable, agentType, executionMode, optional parentId, workflowRunId, factoryRunId
subagent.configured data: model, reasoningEffort, contextTier, multiTurn
subagent.selected data: agentName, agentDisplayName, tools (the definition declared list)

subagent.completed data: toolCallId, agentName, agentDisplayName, model, firstDispatchedModel, configuredModelPreference, modelSelectionSource, configuredModelMatchesActual, totalToolCalls, totalTokens, durationMs and optional explicitModelOverride, explicitModelMatchesPreference, modelOverrideReason, cancelled
subagent.failed carries the same provenance fields plus error
subagent.deselected has empty data
session.background_tasks_changed has empty data and fires on each background-task transition
workflow.run_started, workflow.run_settled and workflow.run_updated carry run id, status and consumption
system.notification kinds are agent_completed, agent_idle, new_inbox_message and workflow_completed

Observed order for one child: subagent.started, subagent.configured, subagent.selected, then the child user.message, assistant.turn_start, model and tool events, assistant.turn_end and subagent.completed; the persisted log also holds a child system.message and session.model_change
session.tasks methods: startAgent, register, update, list, refresh, waitForPending, getProgress, getCurrentPromotable, promoteToBackground, promoteCurrentToBackground, cancel, remove, sendMessage
session.tools has updateSubagentSettings and initializeAndValidate (invoked by subagent sessions that need initialized tools before send)
session.fleet.start and session.agent list, select, deselect, getCurrent, reload, setPrompt complete the set

Settings keys: subagents.agents, subagents.disabledSubagents, subagents.maxConcurrency, subagents.maxDepth, subagents.contextManagementTools, builtInAgents.rubberDuck, builtInAgents.rubberDuckAutoInvoke, workflows.maxConcurrentRuns, workflows.logPhaseNames, workflows.defaultLimits
sub_agents is a legacy settings alias that maps to subagents

The /settings screen hides subagents.** and builtInAgents.** except maxConcurrency, maxDepth and contextManagementTools; the rest is edited in /subagents; workflows.defaultLimits is hidden unless dynamic workflows are enabled
COPILOT_EVENTS_LOG_DIRECTORY sets the events log directory
COPILOT_TASK_WAIT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS sets the non-interactive wait for background tasks
EXECUTION_SUBAGENT_MODEL, EXECUTION_SUBAGENT_MAX_TURNS, SEARCH_SUBAGENT_MODEL and SEARCH_SUBAGENT_MAX_TURNS configure the execution and search subagents
COPILOT_DEBUG_ENABLE_SIDEKICKS, COPILOT_CLI_ENABLED_FEATURE_FLAGS and COPILOT_EXPERIMENTS are debug and flag overrides; COPILOT_DETACHED_SESSION marks the shutdown rem-agent process
Feature flags: copilot_cli_rubber_duck_gpt_claude (RUBBER_DUCK_AGENT) gates rubber-duck and COPILOT_SUBCONSCIOUS gates rem-agent and the subconscious sidekick
Feature flags copilot_cli_execution_subagent, copilot_cli_execution_subagent_model and copilot_cli_search_subagent_model gate the specialized tools
Prompt variant flags STABILITY_ORDERED_SYSTEM_PROMPT_V2, OMIT_DOCS_INSTRUCTION, NARROW_SCOPE_DIRECTIVES and VERIFICATION_STOPPING_RULE select prompt variants
Gotcha: the declared creation methods and wrappers look live but have no callers so a spawn is not traceable through them
Gotcha: subagent.selected lists declared tools, not effective tools
Gotcha: the required model policy overrides the model argument and the YAML list so pinned built-ins run on one model
Gotcha: a background task call in a batch with a sync call gets its started result only when the batch ends
Gotcha: a finished background agent reports idle, not completed, and the idle notification UI text says completed
